welcome_text: Sign in to your Theca server to sync its libraries with folders on this computer.
login_device_hint: How this computer appears in your account's app passwords.
default_folder_hint: Where the account's libraries go, each in a folder of its name.
login_waiting: Your browser opened to approve this device. Check the page in your browser shows:
remove_account_text: Every folder of this account stops syncing and this device is signed out. Deleting removes only files identical to the server's; anything else is kept.
signed_out: This device was signed out of {instance}.
locate_title: This isn't the folder that was synced
locate_text: Sync {library} with it anyway? Its files will be merged with the library.
remove_text: Its folder stays on this computer unless you delete the files. Deleting removes only files identical to the server's; anything else is kept.
offered_hint: Too big to sync by themselves, or declined before.
libraries_none: Every library of this account is synced.
merge_text: They'll be merged with {library}: identical files kept, different ones become new versions.
first_text: Signed in as {email}. Each library can be synced to a folder, kept as a drive (all shown, downloaded when opened), or left: nothing is added until you choose.
new_limit_hint: A larger one is shown, with a notification. 0: no limit.
drive_hint: Show the whole library, download a file when it's opened, keep downloads within the drive limit.
drive_switch_on: macOS added this drive switched off: switch it on in System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → File Providers → Theca.
drive_kept_none: Nothing is kept: files are downloaded when opened, and may be freed again.
drive_limit_hint: How much downloaded content all drives keep on this computer, kept files and edits not uploaded yet aside: the least recently used go first.
drive_limit_default: the default: 10 GiB, or a tenth of the disk if smaller
logs_saved: Saved: it applies the next time Theca starts.
logs_hint: What Theca did, a file per day, to read or send when something goes wrong. They name your files, never your passwords. Changes apply the next time Theca starts.
autostart: Start Theca when you log in
